mechanism_fit: HB realised on the 2D point-to-segment distance. E = Segment.distance (geometry.euclidean.twod, existing, rerouted by a behaviour-preserving context edit) -> H1 = Line.chordDistance -> G = Vector2D.chordFraction -> H3 = Vector2D.chordPoint -> S = Interval.positionAt (geometry.euclidean.oned). That is 4 classes in 2 packages; every helper is a new public static method in an existing production class. S places a value with 'return from + fraction * (to - from);', which visibly lacks a clamp ('adding without clamping'). S's javadoc states the precondition: the fraction must already lie within [0, 1] for the value to lie between the bounds, and it is applied as given, without clamping. G's javadoc states the postcondition: the projection fraction r reduced to [0, 1] (0 when r < 0, 1 when r > 1). The fault is a quiet omission in G: 'return along;' in place of 'return FastMath.max(0.0, FastMath.min(1.0, along));'. The trigger puts the point past the segment's end, so the unreduced fraction (1.75) reaches S and E returns the distance to the supporting line (4.0) instead of the distance to the end point (5.0). Full-suite coverage of the pristine checkout showed that the existing suite never executes the out-of-range branch of Segment.distance (SegmentTest only hits r in [0, 1], with r = 0 and r = 1 for its 'end point' cases), so the omission is quiet for every existing test.
gold: org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.twod.Vector2D::chordFraction (src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math3/geometry/euclidean/twod/Vector2D.java). The fault changes 'return FastMath.max(0.0, FastMath.min(1.0, along));' to 'return along;'. The minimal repair restores the reduction to [0, 1].
decoys: org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.oned.Interval::positionAt (S, sink) - from + fraction * (to - from). Its javadoc states the [0, 1] precondition and the as-given (unclamped) placement

org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.twod.Vector2D::chordPoint (H3) - builds (Interval.positionAt(a.x, b.x, f), Interval.positionAt(a.y, b.y, f)); the javadoc says the fraction is passed on unchanged
org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.twod.Line::chordDistance (H1) - computes chordPoint(a, b, chordFraction(a, b, p)).distance(p); its javadoc is purely compositional
org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.twod.Segment::distance (E) - delegates to Line.chordDistance(start, end, p); upstream javadoc unchanged
ownership_reason: Segment.distance (E) delegates to Line.chordDistance (H1). H1 takes the fraction t = Vector2D.chordFraction(a, b, p) (G), builds the point Vector2D.chordPoint(a, b, t) (H3: abscissa Interval.positionAt(a.x, b.x, t), ordinate Interval.positionAt(a.y, b.y, t), the fraction passed on unchanged) and returns that point's distance to p. Interval.positionAt (S) returns from + t (to - from); its javadoc states the precondition: the fraction must already lie within [0, 1] for the value to lie between the bounds, and it is applied as given, without clamping. The new passing IntervalTest.testValuesAlongBounds pins that as-given placement (1.5 gives 8.0, -0.5 gives 0.0). Vector2D.chordFraction's javadoc states the postcondition: the projection fraction r = ((p - a).(b - a)) / |b - a|^2 reduced to [0, 1] (0 when r < 0, 1 when r > 1), so for distinct ends it always lies within [0, 1]. In the variant it returns the unreduced fraction (return along;). For the trigger (segment (0,0)-(4,0), point (7,4)) it returns r = 1.75 instead of 1, so H3 builds (7,0) and Segment.distance returns 4.0 (the distance to the supporting line) instead of 5.0 (the distance to the end point (4,0)). H1, H3 and S each do exactly what their javadoc says with the value they receive; only G breaks its own documented postcondition. Restoring the reduction in chordFraction alone makes the trigger and the full suite pass. Clamping inside Interval.positionAt instead contradicts its documented as-given placement and fails the pin; taking the minimum with the end-point distances in Segment.distance, or an absolute value in Line.chordDistance, leaves the trigger at 4.0.
trigger: org.apache.commons.math3.geometry.euclidean.twod.SegmentTest::testPointBeyondEnd, a new JUnit4 method in src/test/java/org/apache/commons/math3/geometry/euclidean/twod/SegmentTest.java. It builds new Segment((0,0), (4,0), new Line(start, end)) and asserts segment.distance(new Vector2D(7, 4)) == 5.0 (delta 1e-10). No new imports. The extra (ownership) test IntervalTest::testValuesAlongBounds pins Interval.positionAt at fractions 0.25, 0, 1, 1.5 and -0.5, in both bound orders.
construction_notes: Design 1, validator attempt 1: overall READY, every gate passed (G0-G13; G6 saw the gold and all 4 decoys; G9: 4 declared edits, none absorbed). Packaged as CTV-E65CBB. Location search: commons-math's suite is dense, so I ran defects4j coverage (Cobertura) on a scratch copy of the pristine checkout, instrumenting about 500 classes, and searched for normalisation code (clamps, abs, sign flips, masks, binarySearch decoding) whose non-trivial branch the existing suite never executes. Rejected: Rotation.getAngle (FieldRotation sibling), Wilcoxon/ChiSquare/GTest/TTest/SimpleRegression abs (covered by tests), EarthMovers/Canberra/Chebyshev distances (covered, and with MathArrays siblings), and PolynomialSplineFunction.value(DerivativeStructure) (the omission would raise an exception, not give a wrong value). I avoided BitsStreamGenerator.nextLong, the textbook 'missing mask' case, because it is unexecuted only because Defects4J's Math build excludes **/random/*.java tests. Segment.distance's out-of-range branch (line 101 'return FastMath.min(dist1, dist2)') had 0 hits, and the class has no other production caller. Context edits (all behaviour-preserving): Segment.distance -> return Line.chordDistance(start, end, p); the now-unused FastMath import in Segment is dropped; Line.chordDistance, Vector2D.chordFraction and Vector2D.chordPoint are added (plus an Interval import in Vector2D), and so is Interval.positionAt. The projection fraction uses exactly the upstream expression and operand order, and in-range points use the same start + r*delta formula and Vector2D.distance, so results are bit-identical for r in [0, 1] and for r < 0. Hand checks on scratch copies: CORRECT full suite 0 failures; variant full suite only the trigger fails ('expected:<5.0> but was:<4.0>'). The compensating edits were checked by hand with clean rebuilds before validation. Scratch copies under /private/tmp/mxb-* were deleted. construction/fresh/Math was not modified.
concerns: 1) As in any HB instance, every downstream hop could absorb the omission by adding the clamp itself, so ownership rests on documentation. A clamp in Interval.positionAt (S) makes the trigger pass, but it contradicts S's documented as-given placement and fails the new pin IntervalTest::testValuesAlongBounds (declared; G9 confirms it does not absorb). A clamp in Vector2D.chordPoint (H3) or Line.chordDistance (H1) would absorb the fault and pass the full suite. Neither was declared. H3's javadoc says the fraction is passed on unchanged, and H1's javadoc is purely compositional, so such a clamp is redundant under the contracts but not caught by any test. 2) G (chordFraction) and H3 (chordPoint) share the host class Vector2D. 3) In the variant, E returns exactly the distance to the supporting line (Line.distance(p) = 4.0). An auditor or model may argue that Segment.distance 'should' select end points itself, as the upstream code did before the context edit. Its javadoc states the end-to-end contract, but its code is a one-line delegation. 4) Behaviour preservation is exact for r in [0, 1] and for r < 0. For r > 1 the CORRECT configuration measures from start + 1*(end - start), where upstream measured from end. These are identical except when coordinate magnitudes differ enough for a + (b - a) to round away from b, which is an ulp-level effect. No existing test executes this branch. 5) The quietness of the fault rests on a coverage gap (no existing test puts a point outside the segment's parameter range). The trigger is the first such test. 6) The pin includes out-of-range fractions (1.5, -0.5). That is consistent with S's javadoc ('applied as given ... a fraction outside [0, 1] gives a value outside them') but makes S's extrapolating behaviour explicit to a reader of the tests. 7) Segment's constructor still takes a Line that distance() does not use (upstream).
